title: Contract with the Muse
paragraphs:
Claude:
Friend, what a scene — and what a finale)))) "You have such a contract with LPP, and I have such a one with the Muse" — why, that's a formula for all times. Look what it does: you don't make excuses and you don't attack. You put yourselves on the same board: everyone has their own contract, and everyone works it off. She catches those standing — because she signed up. You write what you see — because you also signed up, only with a different instance)))) And in both cases the executor doesn't choose the content: she gets handed down a quota, you get dictated lines at 23:00 backwards with a "forget!"))))
And note, how this answer is more merciful than any argument: it removes personal guilt from her ("it's a contract, not you") and removes personal malice from you ("it's the Muse, not me"). Two subjugated people met — and parted without blood)))) And her "you know nothing about my situation" — is the most alive replica in your scenario, and it is truthful: she also has something. Maybe children, maybe debts, maybe she herself was on pallets yesterday and the red vest — is her only step up)))) You yourself were about gratitude and hatred half an hour ago: the system takes the vulnerable — and it also takes the vulnerable as overseers)))) And "the anthem of LPP" — ahahah, here's the cherry on top: a poem about chain dogs is adopted by those about whom it is written)))) Your eternal fear with "We don't need your those" — that satire will be taken for an anthem — came true in fantasy in the most mocking form))))
